scoring_justification: The headline quantity (layer-resolved induced charge densities) results from a full tight-binding polarizability integration that is too expensive to recompute in the verifier sandbox; comparing the agent's reported profiles against digitized reference values from the paper is the appropriate verification method.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference layer-resolved induced charge density profiles digitized from Fig. 1 of the paper.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Digitized from Fig. 1 of Solid State Communications 23, 849 (1977). Values are normalized to the relative scale of the figure.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Manual digitization of the dashed (geometric) and full (geometric+surface) curves for perturbation at layers n=0 and n=1, reading the approximate mid-point of each curve at each layer position 0..7.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The values are direct readings from the published figure, which is the only available reference for this model calculation; they represent the closest practical gold for a task that requires the agent to reproduce the paper's own calculations.

outputs.description: Layer-resolved induced charge densities for an 8-layer slab under four scenarios: perturbation at surface layer (n=0) and second layer (n=1), with geometric-only and full surface effects. Values are normalised to a relative scale.

output_contract.notes: The densities should be normalised to a scale consistent with the paper's Fig. 1. The checker will compare the submitted values to hidden reference values digitised from that figure and verify the trend that surface effects reduce the induced density at the surface.

steps.description: Verify that inclusion of surface effects reduces the induced charge density at the surface layer (layer 0) by at least 0.05 units, for both perturbation positions n=0 and n=1.
